videos.title: Insight 2021, 4 Oct 21, Event 1 - Welcome and opening event: 'A brave new world'
videos.description:
'A brave new world: Should health and care systems trust algorithms?'
In our first session, we discussed ‘how health and care systems should respond to the rise of patient facing Artificial Intelligence tools’ with our diverse panel Andi Orlowski (Health Economics Unit), Farzana Hussain (GP and Clinical Director), Reena Sangar (Ipsos MORI) and Mike Emery (Hereford and Worcester CCG) who debated this fascinating and important subject to start our festival on 'Insight to Action'

videos.title: Insight 2021, 5 Oct 21, Event 2 - What can we learn from the pandemic to reduce health inequalities?
videos.description:
The COVID pandemic has highlighted the stark inequalities in health that exist in the UK and globally. This session will reflect on some of the learning from the NHS frontline in Bradford and how data, science and community engagement was harnessed to protect a city.

There is a second pandemic that is killing far more people than COVID  - that of non-communicable disease. There are no simple vaccines or silver bullets for this pandemic. The solutions lie in tackling the wider determinants of health that interact in our complex social and urban systems.

The session will describe one example of how a systems approach is being trialled that focuses on prevention rather than cures.

videos.title: Insight 2021, 6 Oct 21, Event 4: Insight to action – what works?
videos.description: It has been estimated that it can take up to 17 years to translate evidence into practice - how can we change that?  Join us to hear from a diverse panel of speakers who will share their experiences of research and practice across a range of sectors. Learn about what works (and what doesn't!) in different contexts and what happens when well conceived plans meet reality.

videos.title: Insight 2021, 11 Oct 2021, Event 7 - Sharing your awesomeness
videos.description: The session will look at how we can put insight into action through remarkable stories, working with communication teams, spreading your ideas and standing out from the crowd.

videos.title: Festival Launch - new perspectives on analysis and decision making
videos.description:
https://midlandsdecisionsupport.nhs.uk/
https://www.strategyunitwm.nhs.uk/

Our Festival journey begins with the Strategy Unit team setting the scene on the importance of analytics, evaluation and evidence in addressing the current challenges facing health and care and supporting better decision-making – followed by two perspectives from our keynote speakers, Ben Goldacre and Andi Orlowski.

Ben Goldacre will describe how open approaches can revolutionise health data science in the UK. Ben is a doctor, academic, writer, and broadcaster. He trained in medicine at Oxford and UCL, in psychiatry at the Maudsley, and in epidemiology at LSHTM. His academic and policy work is in informatics, epidemiology and evidence based medicine, where he works on various problems including variation in care, better uses of routinely collected electronic health data, evidence-based social policy, access to clinical trial data, efficient trial design, and retracted papers. His talk will explore key ways in which we can bring NHS data analysis into the 21st century and the value of ‘open by default’ approaches such as the OpenSAFELY analytics platform in advancing analytical collaboration across health and care.

This will be followed by Andi Orlowski who will be exploring "Dangerous analytics…and how local analysts can save you!". Andi is a health economist and a national advisor for population health management (PHM).  Andi starts his new role in October as Director of the Health Economics Unit at MLCSU, a new team working alongside and in collaboration with the Strategy Unit.  His talk will include an exploration of the potential pitfalls and perils of analytics – the ways in which analysis can miss the point, can contribute to worsening inequalities and potentially cause harm. It will also highlight the value of working closely with local analysts to overcome these challenges and make better decisions.

Both talks will be highly interactive and participants will have the opportunity to engage with two leading experts and gain insight into some of the latest perspectives on the use of analysis in health and care. The Strategy Unit’s Professor Mohammed A Mohammed will be on hand to host a Q&A with our speakers and to support the discussion.

The session will close with a brief guide to navigating the festival and upcoming festival sessions. This session will be of interest to anyone who wants to see better use of analysis to support decision-making and we encourage all festival participants to take part in this opening session.

videos.description:

Social care services have had to change rapidly in the face of the challenge of COVID-19.  At the same time, the preferences and choices of those services have also changed. The market for care provision is also heavily impacted.

This panel discussion will consider what has changed; what has been learned so far; what should be kept and built on; and what the future now holds; and what that all means for integrated working. 
The discussion will be chaired by Professor Robin Miller (Head of Department Social Work and Social Care, University of Birmingham) and Robin will be joined by Natasha Curry (Acting Deputy Director of Policy, Nuffield Trust) who has an interest in international health and social care systems and is leading the Trust’s work on social care.

videos.title: INSIGHT 2020:  Introduction by Peter Spilsbury, Director of the Strategy Unit
videos.description:
Insight 2020, hosted by the Strategy Unit, 6-week Festival of over 30 virtual events held from September to November 2020.  The Festival explored some of the challenges facing decision-makers in health and care in 2020 and beyond; emerging models of practice to make best use of analysis to inform decision-making and some of the exciting work already happening in this area.  Insight 2020 featured a mixture of events, workshops, panels and conversations at a local, national and international level. Most of the events were recorded and are available on YouTube and via the Decision Support Centre website (see below).

In this video Peter Spilsbury (Director, the Strategy Unit) introduces the Insight 2020 Festival, describing what it's all about and why we decided to do this.  

Week 1: Our decision-making context in 2020
Transformation in health and care has been rapid and intensive, particularly in 2020.  Asking the right analytical questions requires joined-up approaches, between leaders and their analytical workforce, as well as broader system stakeholders. This week’s theme focused on the vital issues facing decision-makers, the contexts they are operating in, and from where they might draw support.

Week 2: The role of the Decision Support Network
The Midlands Decision Support Unit (DSU) Network is a new and emerging approach to bring together analytical resource across a region, develop analytical skills collectively and share learning from analytical projects. This week’s theme describes how the network will operate, shares some of the learning from systems who have adopted this approach already and describes how evidence will underpin the Network's approach to decision-making.

Week 3: Analytical Priorities of the Decision Support Network
The Midlands Decision Support Unit Network has defined its analytical priorities for 20/21. This week’s theme described the projects being carried out on behalf of the Network to respond to these priorities, the outputs they will produce and how these will be shared with the DSU Network and its partners. This included the presentation of work already completed on behalf of the Network, focusing on resource usage in the last two years of life. This week we also considered: what this way of working means for the future of analytics – what opportunities could it create for our analysts, our leaders and our population?

Week 4: Exploring health inequalities
COVID-19 has shone a light on health inequalities; it has “laid bare our longstanding social, economic and political inequalities…” (BMJ, 2020) and this is against a backdrop of declining life expectancy in our poorest communities, well before COVID-19. The Marmot review 10 years on found that regional and socioeconomic differences in health are large and growing. Michael Marmot describes this as ‘shocking’ and that we should work towards creating the conditions for everyone to be able to lead lives they have reason to value.

During this week’s theme we shared a special selection of events which looked at health inequalities through very different lenses. We considered where health inequalities exist, what we have learned during the COVID-19 pandemic and what we are doing to address them that we need to amplify?

Week 5: The Decision-making toolbox
Decision-making is an art; we can train at it, rehearse and access tools to support us. However, humans are also subject to a wide range of biases which can undermine the quality of decision making, especially in complex real-world systems. This week’s theme focused on the range of materials that exist to help us be better decision-makers.  We also thought about how we make best use of resources to collect the right evidence to support our decision-making, ensuring our methods are tested and reviewed with the aim of continuous improvement. 

Week 6: Making the most of our decision-making resources
The final week’s theme was a reflection on what had been heard in the previous weeks. We thought about how we develop our analytical leaders by building on the success of the Midlands Population Health Management Academy and thought conceptually about ‘what makes a good decision?’, drawing on the tools and techniques shown over the course of the Festival. Concluded by an expert panel who considered where we go from here…

videos.title: INSIGHT 2020: Event 18 - Homelessness and Covid 19 using research to learn in a crisis
videos.description:
Insight 2020, hosted by the Strategy Unit, was a 6-week Festival of over 30 virtual events held from September to November 2020.  The Festival explored some of the challenges facing decision-makers in health and care in 2020 and beyond; emerging models of practice to make best use of analysis to inform decision-making and some of the exciting work already happening in this area.

Insight 2020 featured a mixture of events, workshops, panels and conversations at a local, national and international level. Most of the events were recorded and are available on YouTube.

Context:
Covid-19 brought crisis to many people already in crisis. For people experiencing homelessness it led to radical changes in circumstance, not least as the ‘everyone in’ policy changed their housing situation.  Health and care services also had to make radical changes in their operation. This provided an opportunity to learn. Of these changes, which represented improvements on previous practice? Which were a step back? Which needed further evaluation?

During this session we hear about the experiences of research teams from homelessness charity Groundswell and the Strategy Unit. Both had been asked to gather evidence to provide decision makers - in NHS England and NHS Improvement (NHSE/I), and elsewhere – with the insights they needed to learn from the health and care response to homelessness during COVID-19.

Speakers: Olivia Butterworth (Head of Public Participation for NHS England and NHS Improvement), Jenny McAteer (Directs Groundswell’s national #HealthNow project), Jo Brown (Research Manager at Groundswell) and Fraser Battye (The Strategy Unit)

videos.title: INSIGHT 2020: Event 19 - The trauma impact of COVID 19 on children and young people - how to respond
videos.description:
Insight 2020, hosted by the Strategy Unit, was a 6-week Festival of over 30 virtual events held from September to November 2020.  The Festival explored some of the challenges facing decision-makers in health and care in 2020 and beyond; emerging models of practice to make best use of analysis to inform decision-making and some of the exciting work already happening in this area.

Insight 2020 featured a mixture of events, workshops, panels and conversations at a local, national and international level.  Most of the events were recorded and are available on YouTube.


Context:
Whilst for children and young people the direct impact of COVID-19 has been limited, the impact of COVID-19 on family and society and the experience of lockdown have both been profound in their effects. It seems certain that many children and young people have experienced trauma as a result of the pandemic and our response to it. In addition, we know that children’s use of even urgent health services during COVID fell dramatically, with parents /guardians making difficult choices in the face of uncertainty about relative risks. The question of whether that represents a latent pool of harm or instead a falling away of  demand that was ‘cautionary but not necessary’  is still to be properly answered.

This session, "The Trauma of COVID-19 - a creative response to the effects of the pandemic and lockdown on children and young people" was an open exploration of the range of trauma that has been experienced, its possible implications and how we as a society/ suite of public services need to respond to that and be creative in so doing.

Speakers: Dr. Ingrid Wolfe (Chair, Consultant in paediatrics and public health; Director, Institute for Women’s and Children’s Health, Kings Health Partners) Nigel Osborne (Composer, researcher and international aid worker, Sally Rowe (Executive Director of Children’s Services, Walsall Council), Swaran Singh (Professor of Social and Community Psychiatry, University of Warwick) and Peter Spilsbury (Director, The Strategy Unit)

videos.title: INSIGHT 2020: Event 24  - Insight 2020 and NHS-R: Why the NHS and care system should use R
videos.description:
About Insight 2020:
Insight 2020, hosted by the Strategy Unit, was a 6-week Festival of over 30 virtual events held from September to November 2020.  The Festival explored some of the challenges facing decision-makers in health and care in 2020 and beyond; emerging models of practice to make best use of analysis to inform decision-making and some of the exciting work already happening in this area.

Insight 2020 featured a mixture of events, workshops, panels and conversations at a local, national and international level.

Background
R is free, it’s highly sharable and is backed up by a community of R users who love to help and apparently when you get the R bug – you’re hooked! There are so many examples of its potential and the opportunities to ultimately improve care and outcomes.  But this doesn’t ‘just happen’ and the aim is to dramatically increase the use of R especially within the NHS but to realize the potential, to see the explosion in quality, shared analytics – we need many more people to understand why and how this can happen. We are on a bit of a mission to hugely increase the use of R because we think it’s that important! In this event we do our best to share the value of R and how it could help you, your organization and your patients or users.

This event:
This was a joint event between the Insight 2020 Festival and the 3rd NHS-R Conference. The session introduced R - the open source programming language that’s used widely in finance and academia and is now being used more and more in health and care.

Insight 2020, hosted by the Strategy Unit, was a 6-week Festival of over 30 virtual events held from September to November 2020. To close the Insight 2020 Festival, we brought together a remarkable panel of leaders to discuss how decision quality could be improved in the new NHS.  The panel reflected on:

• The nature of the decision-making challenge ahead and questions of legitimacy in decision-making that we are seeing emerge across society at present;
• What they see as the essential ingredients of decision-making and leadership in ICSs that are capable of maintaining the confidence of the public and the workforce, and are up to the task of optimizing the value achieved from the resources available to the NHS (and partners);
• The role they see for learning systems and networks (such as the Midlands DSU Network) in supporting them; 
• What principles should be held dearest by leaders of health and care systems as we chart our way through COVID-19.

Speakers: Peter Spilsbury, (The Strategy Unit), Sally Warren (Kings Fund), Danielle Oum (Walsall Healthcare NHS Trust) and Andy Williams (Leicester, Leicestershire & Rutland CCG’s)

Insight 2020 featured a mixture of events, workshops, panels and conversations at a local, national and international level.

This video: Event 25 – The Decision Support Unit Education & Development Programme

Analytics is increasingly featuring in complex decision-making processes and more is now expected of our analyst workforce, but finding relevant, practical, high quality training and development solutions is challenging.  The Decision Support Unit Network will address this challenge by providing central training and development opportunities for analysts and leaders.

In this session, Professor Mohammed A Mohammed and colleagues, describe our planned series of cutting-edge Action Learning Sets (ALS) aimed at both the technical and leadership development of our analyst community so that we can bring analytics to the heart of the decision making process.  This incudes topics such as systems dynamics, quasi-experimental design, machine learning and leadership development.

In this video, Professor Al Mulley, managing director of the Dartmouth Institute’s Global Health Care Delivery Science Program, addresses the challenge of measurably improving decision quality by considering the interdependence of the dialogues that take place between:

(1) patients and clinicians;
(2) policy makers or managers and clinicians; and 
(3) policy makers and citizens.

An interesting session which will help you think differently about the quality of decisions made at the levels of the patient, the service organization, and the health and care system.
